title: The Field Across the Fence: The Unchosen Path

features.name: fence-that-holds-both-times
features.desc-on-touch: The fence doesn't separate the paths so much as hold them both true at once. On each side, the grass wears the footsteps of a life you didn't live, but the earth remembers both.

features.name: fenceposts-measuring-parallel-time
features.desc-on-touch: Each post is carved with years—but the years don't match between sides. One fence-line ages faster. Or perhaps differently.

features.name: the-standing-place
features.desc-on-touch: Standing here with her, watching both paths open downslope. She asked which one to take and you both knew the earth would remember you taking both.

features.name: crossroads-seen-as-one
features.desc-on-touch: From far enough away the two paths look like they were always the same path, just doubling back. Close enough and you see they were never the same twice.

features.name: weather-vane-spinning-both-ways
features.desc-on-touch: The vane points north on this side, south on that. Or perhaps it's pointing at what you chose and what chose to go on without you.

inscription: both paths home; you chose once but the earth keeps the score of twice

file.name: Parallel_Life_Journal_Undated.tmp
file.note: A journal fragment that seems to describe events that didn't happen here, but happened across the fence. The handwriting is yours but the choices are all different.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the fence at dusk
narr: you stand here with her at the split, both paths golden
stretching downslope. she asks which one home is and you
point. then you point the other way. the fence holds both
directions true. that's when you see the grass is equally worn
on both sides—equally walked into, equally remembered by the land
you didn't choose one life. the earth chose to keep both for you.

exits.label: back across the fence to the mirror field
upslope where both paths seem to lead
into the dark where the unchosen path goes deepest
